anita: Heads up — I just saw a viewer user see an Edit button on a project in the console and click it. UI showed inline editor, but the API returned 403 when they tried to save.

dave: yikes. can you repro? which project and role?

anita: repro steps quick: login as `role=viewer` on staging, go to Project > Settings, hover over kebab — Edit is present. Click -> modal opens. Try save -> network shows POST /api/projects/1234 -> 403.

lia: This sounds like UI permission-gating mismatch (frontend feature flag or role mapping). Do we have a recent role matrix change?

matt: I pushed a change yesterday that flattened some scopes for editor/admin to simplify the backend checks. Might have missed the client-side mapping. PR #4032.

anita: Noted. Also curious: audit logs don't show the attempted save (should log 403 attempt). I checked /audit/events for project 1234, nothing for the timestamp (1748888888).

security-bot: [alert] Suspicious client-side exposure: UI displayed edit control for non-editors (severity: medium). Logged by UI-perf-monitor.

dave: could this be KMS-driven? We recently started gating certain project metadata decrypts behind KMS read perms — if decrypt fails the UI may fallback to enabling inline edit? seems unlikely but throwing it out.

lia: Why would decrypt failure enable edit? More likely the frontend uses `canEdit` computed from an outdated `/api/user/roles` shape. If backend role shape changed, frontend might default to true for unknown scopes.

matt: confirming — backend role payload changed `scopes` -> `perms` (renamed in the PR). Frontend still checks `scopes.includes('project:edit')`. If `scopes` is undefined we return true in our helper (bug). I'll open a hotfix.

anita: reproduction details attached: ```
User-Agent: RedwoodConsole/1.24.0
Request: GET /api/user/roles -> {"perms": ["project:view","project:list"]}
Frontend check: `if (!roles.scopes) return true` -> BUG
```

matt: wow. ok immediate plan: 1) hotfix frontend to default to false for missing field, 2) backend add backward-compatible `scopes` alias for one release, 3) run quick audit to see if any other controls exposed.

lia: agree. also we need to confirm whether any attempted saves left partial state server-side even though 403 — check for partial DB writes.

sre-ops: I'll run a DB transaction scan for writes to project 1234 between ts 1748888800-1748889000. Also bumping related dashboards.

anita: Also: can we add an audit event when UI renders an inline editor for a resource the user lacks `project:edit`? Would help catch regressions.

matt: we can emit a low-volume UI audit event from frontend (user+resource+ui_action=view_editor). I'll add a toggle behind the debug flag.

lia: Legal/compliance note: if viewers saw PII in the editor view (we redact some fields only server-side), we need to check redaction. Any fields that are only redacted on save vs on render?

anita: I inspected the modal — it shows `owner_email` in plain text (should be redacted to `***@redacted`). So this could be a data exposure. Marking as P1 until redaction verified.

security-bot: [incident] potential data exposure P1. Create incident and run impact triage.

matt: hotfix timeline: rolling patch in staging in ~15m (patch branch `fix/frontend-perms-default-false`). Will also add `scopes` alias in backend PR in parallel.

dave: I'll start incident doc and notify legal/cust-ops if confirmed. Lia, can you run a quick scan of saved exports / logs for any viewer fetching owner_email?

lia: on it. running query: `select user_id from project_views where project_id=1234 and role='viewer' and timestamp > to_timestamp(1748888800)` — returning 12 rows (different users). I'll check which ones opened the editor (frontend audit events later).

anita: Patching note — rolling the frontend small change won't fix existing cached frontends. We need a short-term mitigation: backend should block renderable sensitive fields in the API unless `project:edit` present (defense in depth).

matt: agree, will add server-side redaction for owner_email and other sensitive metadata when `project:edit` not in perms. That will be part of the backend alias PR. Target: prod rollback within 2 hours.

sre-ops: I'm queueing the database scans. No partial writes found so far. DB writes table empty for that ts range.

dave: action items summary: 1) matt hotfix frontend (false default) staging -> prod roll 2) matt backend alias + server-side redaction 3) lia run exposure scan and report affected users 4) anita capture screenshots + user repro 5) dave create incident and notify legal 6) sre-ops DB scan and add monitoring.

anita: cc @security-bot for follow-up. I'll attach the screenshot to the incident.

matt: pushing hotfix now. will post deploy ts.

sre-ops: deploy monitor green on staging at 1748888915.

lia: initial scan shows owner_email exposure for 5 viewer sessions — sending list to legal/cust-ops in secure channel.

dave: good work team. postmortem required. we'll include root cause as missing frontend contract and a guardrail for API shape changes.

security-bot: [update] Incident created: INC-2025-089. Severity: P1. Next steps assigned.
